title: Resilient Microservice Traffic Distribution
business: Organizations running distributed web services that require high availability and consistent backend health monitoring.
problem: Manual traffic routing often leads to downtime when individual backend nodes fail, as traffic continues to be routed to unresponsive services, causing user-facing errors.
solution: HAProxy acts as a reverse proxy that performs active health checks on backend servers and distributes traffic based on defined load balancing algorithms, ensuring requests only reach healthy instances.
steps: Define a backend section in the configuration file specifying the list of available server nodes.
Configure health check parameters within the server lines to monitor service availability via periodic requests.
Set a load balancing algorithm, such as round-robin, to distribute incoming traffic across the healthy server pool.
Configure the frontend to receive incoming client traffic and route it to the defined backend.
Validate the configuration using the HAProxy CLI to ensure syntax correctness before applying changes.
outcome: Improved service reliability where traffic is automatically diverted away from failing nodes, resulting in a seamless user experience during backend maintenance or outages.
limitation: Active health checks consume network resources and backend processing capacity; monitor the frequency of checks to ensure they do not become a source of overhead for the backend services.

questions.question: In Resilient Microservice Traffic Distribution, what is the primary role of the reverse proxy?
options: To perform active health checks and distribute traffic to healthy nodes
To replace the backend database entirely
To encrypt all client-side traffic automatically
To increase the hardware capacity of the backend servers
questions.explanation: The solution relies on HAProxy's ability to monitor backend health and route traffic only to functional instances.
questions.evidence: HAProxy acts as a reverse proxy that performs active health checks on backend servers and distributes traffic based on defined load balancing algorithms, ensuring requests only reach healthy instances.

questions.question: In Resilient Microservice Traffic Distribution, what is a key limitation of the implementation?
options: The inability to use round-robin algorithms
The potential for health checks to consume network and backend resources
The requirement to manually restart the proxy for every request
The lack of support for HTTP traffic
questions.explanation: Health checks are not free; they add overhead that must be managed to prevent performance degradation.
questions.evidence: Active health checks consume network resources and backend processing capacity; monitor the frequency of checks to ensure they do not become a source of overhead for the backend services.
